findings.evidence: tasks/reviews/d5_browser_walk.py:88-96 (`vis()`) and :183-193 (the only visibility assertion) — nothing compares the pane rect against the viewport. With `@media(min-width:1001px) and (max-width:1100px){#source{position:relative;left:-9999px}}` appended to index.html's style block, the walk records at 1024 `source: {top:582, left:-9375, width:349, height:636, visible:true, has_offset_parent:true}` while `#pane` sits at left 261 — the compare pane's right edge is at x=-9026, i.e. nothing of it is on screen — and reports `panes_visible: true`, `panes_same_row: true`, `failures: []`, exit 0. `clip-path:inset(100%)` on `#source` is likewise fully green (exit 0, 0 failures). D5's acceptance is worded 'on screen together at 1024x768+', and `checkVisibility` answers 'rendered', not 'on screen'; prompts/019-d5-inspector-layout-and-exclusion-honesty.md calls it 'the native API for the question actually being asked', which overstates it by exactly this gap.
findings.repro: start `uvicorn src.sec10k.web.app:app --port 8011` at d2faf12; insert `@media(min-width:1001px) and (max-width:1100px){#source{position:relative;left:-9999px}}` before `</style>` in src/sec10k/web/static/index.html; `python3 tasks/reviews/d5_browser_walk.py --base http://localhost:8011 --out rv-offscreen` -> exit 0, failures []
findings.acceptance: `measure()` also records whether each pane's rect intersects the viewport (e.g. `r.right > 0 && r.left < innerWidth && r.bottom > 0 && r.top < innerHeight`), and the per-width assertion fails on a non-intersecting pane; the off-viewport mutation above then reports a failure at 1024 and the walk exits 1, while the unmutated tree stays exit 0.
